comparator.name: Earth Sciences (Aardwetenschappen)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–27 OER, checked 2026-09-25; the advertised 2027–28 revision is not substituted for this curriculum
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted OER lists two formal second-year tracks. Aardoppervlak is the first listed and is selected as neutral tie-break between equally substantial Earth-surface and Geologie en Geochemie routes, without reference to UCR. Year 1 is 60 compulsory EC; year 2 is 60 compulsory EC including the five Aardoppervlak-specific units; year 3 comprises 30 compulsory EC (Hydrology 6, Philosophy/History of Science 6, Bachelor thesis 18) and 30 genuinely open academic profiling/minor EC. Zero-credit language test and study/career component are not added. The VU advertises an overhauled programme from 2027–28, whose complete curriculum was not yet published; this record uses the adopted current 2026–27 OER.
components: Duurzaam gebruik van de NL ondergrond
Genuinely open academic 30-EC profiling space; no Earth-science elective is invented.

core: Earth-system processes, climate and landscape change
Soils, water, biogeochemistry and subsurface resources
Geospatial, field, mathematical and statistical Earth-science methods
Earth, life and climate over deep time
adjacent: Geology and geochemistry of the deep Earth
questions: How do Earth subsurface resources and water systems support responsible energy and land decisions?

alternatives.label: Earth systems, water and geoscience resources
alternatives.concept: Studies interacting Earth systems, climate and surface processes through geospatial observation, quantitative models, soils and aquifers, near-surface geochemistry and resource questions. An applied delta project supports research practice; the programme does not reproduce the VU geological field sequence or individual thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The 24 courses emphasize Earth and climate systems, water and soil, geospatial methods and resource questions; the label does not claim a geology degree.
progression: Earth Science, mathematical and sustainability foundations precede Earth modelling, GIS, soils, resource analysis and upper-level biogeochemistry. All formal prerequisites and offered semesters were checked against the 2026 UCR workbook; advisory progression is sensible.

candidates.label: Deep geology, tectonics and planetary geology

routeSelection.basis: The 2026–27 OER confirms two formal tracks; neither is uniquely representative of the broad Earth Sciences target. The first-listed Aardoppervlak track is chosen under the neutral order tie-break and its complete 60-EC second-year path is used. The choice was made without considering UCR fit.

selection.assessment: A second, geology-and-geochemistry-centered curriculum is supported by the formal route and direct interests, but UCR has only introductory deep-Earth work and limited near-surface geochemistry; it cannot supply a different credible 24-course deep geology and tectonics programme. Climate, water, geospatial data and subsurface resources are already substantively included in Alternative 1; no additional distinct direction survives the course and concept gates.

blocks: Earth systems, rocks, climate and landscapes
Both introduce the interacting spheres of the Earth; UCR gives an overview rather than the VU disciplinary sequence.
Both build models of coupled Earth-system processes, though the VU unit belongs to a geological major.
Both address global environmental and climatic change; UCR emphasizes contemporary climate impacts.
Both examine the formation and transformation of landscapes; UCR focuses on coastal and delta settings.

notes.text: The VU Earth Sciences route includes substantial geology, geomorphology, field mapping and an 18-EC individual Earth-science thesis. UCR offers Earth-system, soil, water, climate and geospatial work, but not the same sequence of geological fieldwork or specialist Earth-science depth; its delta research course is a group applied project.
